nodes.label: Transformative Community Project
nodes.description: An integrated model for sustainable forms of learning, working, and living, anchored in a farmstead in Anhalt, East Germany (est. 1884, acquired 2020).

nodes.label: Foundations
nodes.description: The WHY — diagnosis of modern society's problems and the philosophical response.

nodes.label: Alienation & Disintegration
nodes.description: Work alienation, family fragmentation, escapist virtual worlds, loss of meaning. The diagnosis that motivates the project.

nodes.label: Communitarianism
nodes.description: Philosophical framework: decline of values and solidarity under neoliberalism. Preserves individual freedom while embedding people socially.

nodes.label: Active Civil Society
nodes.description: Citizens taking social, economic, and educational responsibility rather than relying solely on state institutions.

nodes.label: From Control Society to Civil Society
nodes.description: Deleuze's concept of the society of control as starting point for reimagining civic agency. Central framing in Ludwik and Ragnar.

nodes.label: Sustainability & UN SDGs
nodes.description: Orientation toward the 2030 Agenda — sustainable development for people, nature, wildlife, and the planet.

nodes.label: Pillars
nodes.description: The WHAT — the five key elements of the transformative model.

nodes.label: Work, Income & Work-Life Balance
nodes.description: Rethinking labor: meaningful work, diverse roles (manual + intellectual), part-time/freelance, self-determination.

nodes.label: Unconditional Basic Income
nodes.description: Financial foundation enabling community participation, entrepreneurship, and social responsibility. Dismantles welfare bureaucracy.

nodes.label: Work-Life Balance
nodes.description: Healthier relationship between work and personal life. Deceleration, reduced commuting, space for contemplation.

nodes.label: Meaningful Labor
nodes.description: Crafts alongside intellectual work, equally valued. Roofers and philosophers, carpenters and educators working together.

nodes.label: Learning & Education
nodes.description: Self-directed, community-oriented learning as alternative to institutional schooling.

nodes.label: Self-Directed Learning
nodes.description: Compulsory schooling converted to self-designed compulsory education. Learners choose their path.

nodes.label: Experiential Education
nodes.description: Learning by doing — Dewey, Hahn, Weikart's HighScope model. Action-oriented, nature-embedded.

nodes.label: Community-Oriented Learning
nodes.description: Intergenerational learning, diverse role models (especially male presence), cooperative skill-building.

nodes.label: Youth Journeying
nodes.description: Adolescents move between projects — farm to mill to urban workshop — self-determined years of exploration. Reimagined apprenticeship.

nodes.label: Entrepreneurship & Community-Building
nodes.description: Reviving abandoned properties, creating local economies, commons-based resource sharing.

nodes.label: Community-Based Enterprise
nodes.description: Entrepreneurial communities in structurally weak areas. Survival skills, cultural adaptation.

nodes.label: The Commons
nodes.description: Shared resources, jointly used land — medieval pastures to modern commons projects. Tension with GDR socialism memory.

nodes.label: Rural Revitalization
nodes.description: Abandoned farms, dairies, vacant properties in East Germany as opportunities for new communities.

nodes.label: Transformation
nodes.description: The binding philosophy — seeing oneself as part of economic, social, cultural, and ecological transformation.

nodes.label: Economic Transformation
nodes.description: From capitalist accumulation toward commons-based, community-embedded economies.

nodes.label: Social Transformation
nodes.description: Rebuilding social cohesion, belonging, intergenerational care. Philosophy of O'Donohue.

nodes.label: Cultural Transformation
nodes.description: Heritage preservation, Polish-German exchange, literature, music, crafts as cultural renewal.

nodes.label: Ecological Transformation
nodes.description: Ecological building materials, organic farming, reduced mobility, climate-positive living.

nodes.label: The Farm in Anhalt
nodes.description: WHERE — the physical project. Three-sided farmstead from 1884, 1h SW of Berlin. Wilhelmine origins, GDR additions.

nodes.label: Buildings
nodes.description: The built structures of the farmstead.

nodes.label: Farmhouse
nodes.description: Living quarters, attic, cellar, three tiled stoves, five chimneys.

nodes.label: Barn
nodes.description: Spacious interior for craft, artistic, educational, cultural activities. Historical windows installed. Hayloft, former chicken coop.

nodes.label: Workshop
nodes.description: Cleaned and redesigned for novel uses. Smart technologies + old manual techniques.

nodes.label: Stables
nodes.description: Former cowshed, horse stable, fodder kitchen. Major reconstruction and extension documented in Ludwik.

nodes.label: Secondary Structures
nodes.description: GDR-era garage, former pigpen, small stalls and sheds (some torn down).

nodes.label: Land & Grounds
nodes.description: Fields, gardens, pastures, terrain.

nodes.label: South Facing Field
nodes.description: Wooden deck fronting the field. Agricultural use.

nodes.label: Gardens
nodes.description: Garden behind the barn. Small horticultural experiments.

nodes.label: Pastures
nodes.description: Grazing land, echoing the medieval commons tradition.

nodes.label: Fruit Trees
nodes.description: Existing fruit trees on the property.

nodes.label: Walnut Tree
nodes.description: Planting, nurturing and caring for a walnut tree — documented as a meditative, long-term act.

nodes.label: Renovation & Construction
nodes.description: The ongoing work of restoring and extending the farmstead.

nodes.label: Heritage Preservation
nodes.description: Preserving Wilhelmine and GDR-era cultural heritage. Historical artifacts, timber-frame techniques.

nodes.label: Ecological Building Materials
nodes.description: Implementing sustainable materials in renovation. Recycling of materials.

nodes.label: Smart Technologies
nodes.description: Linking old manual techniques with new forms of production and technology.

nodes.label: Stable Building Reconstruction
nodes.description: Major reconstruction and extension of the stable building — extensively documented in Ludwik.

nodes.label: Agriculture
nodes.description: Farming activities on the property.

nodes.label: Organic Farming
nodes.description: Ecological agriculture as both livelihood and learning opportunity.

nodes.label: Fruit & Berries
nodes.description: Fruit growing, berries farming. Basis for produce (jams, juices).

nodes.label: Livestock
nodes.description: Sheep farming mentioned. Ecological livestock farming as a project profile.

nodes.label: Horticultural Experiments
nodes.description: Small-scale gardening experiments documented in Ludwik.

nodes.label: Infrastructure
nodes.description: Utilities and systems supporting the farm.

nodes.label: Heat Generation & Timber
nodes.description: Heating systems and timber industry on the farm.

nodes.label: Guttering & Downspouts
nodes.description: Guttering and downspouts for the barn — practical infrastructure work.

nodes.label: Community & People
nodes.description: WHO — the human dimension of the project.

nodes.label: Intergenerational Living
nodes.description: Elders, adults, youth living together. Reduces elder care costs, provides role models.

nodes.label: Village Relations & Mutual Aid
nodes.description: Neighborly structures: farmer helps with tractor, gets field access; firewood exchanged for services.

nodes.label: Diverse Professionals Together
nodes.description: Roofers and philosophers, carpenters and educators, electricians and doctors.

nodes.label: Youth & Adolescents
nodes.description: Ragnar as prototype — young man developing new motivation for learning, working, living. Male adolescents at risk as key demographic.

nodes.label: Polish-German Cultural Exchange
nodes.description: Rooted in Jaczewski's legacy, Krakow connections, Polish literature and language. International scouting ideals.

nodes.label: Life & Conviviality
nodes.description: The social texture of daily life in the think tank — gatherings, meals, shared time.

nodes.label: Creative & Cultural Expression
nodes.description: HOW the project is expressed and documented.

nodes.label: Storytelling & Documentation
nodes.description: Three book volumes, academic article, YouTube channel. Character prototypes (Tomasz, Ludwik, Ragnar) as narrative devices.

nodes.label: Crafts & Making
nodes.description: Furniture making/restoring, jam and juice production, textile design. The jam label as creative act.

nodes.label: Music
nodes.description: Key role of music in the project — documented in Ludwik.

nodes.label: Designs, Objects & Play
nodes.description: Creative design work, object-making, playful experimentation.

nodes.label: Media & Web
nodes.description: Photography (700+ photos across books), YouTube channel, future website. Visual documentation as core practice.

nodes.label: Commercial Dimensions
nodes.description: HOW the project sustains itself economically (future development).

nodes.label: Guest Hosting
nodes.description: Future booking page for hosting guests at the farm. Airbnb-style or independent.

nodes.label: Farm Store / Produce Sales
nodes.description: Selling produce, crafts, goods. Shopify or independent. Jams, juices, organic produce.

nodes.label: Workshops & Events
nodes.description: Seminars, cultural events, educational workshops. Already started (first seminars documented in Tomasz).

nodes.label: Everyday Economy
nodes.description: Day-to-day economic management of the project. Practical sustainability.

nodes.label: Expansion — Vacant Properties
nodes.description: Vision of thousands of similar projects using abandoned properties across East Germany and beyond.
